citation: Landry, S. H., Zucker, T. A., Taylor, H. B., Swank, P. R., Williams, J. M., Assel, M., Crawford, A., Huang, W., Clancy-Menchetti, J., Lonigan, C. J., Phillips, B. M., Eisenberg, N., Spinrad, T. L., de Villiers, J., de Villiers, P., Barnes, M., Starkey, P., & Klein, A. (2014). Enhancing early child care quality and learning for toddlers at risk: The Responsive Early Childhood Program. Developmental Psychology, 50(2), 526-541. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0033494
report_number: Developmental Psychology, 50(2), 526-541; DOI 10.1037/a0033494; PMID 23772822; NICHD grant P01 HD048497
design: Cluster RCT, assignment at classroom/teacher level (one classroom per child-care center). 65 child-care classrooms serving low-income 2- and 3-year-olds (Texas n=34, Florida n=31; ~542 assessed children) randomized to 3 arms: (a) business-as-usual control, (b) RECC = Responsive Early Childhood Curriculum + responsive teaching PD with weekly in-class coaching (37 weeks, ~92 hr), (c) RECC+ = RECC plus an explicit social-emotional curriculum supplement (RECC+ = ~22 teachers, 'one third of the sample'). 5 classrooms exited (2 control, 1 RECC, 2 RECC+) -> 60 classrooms analyzed; per-arm classroom n not tabled in this PDF. Outcomes: child cognitive/achievement (vocabulary EOWPVT, early literacy Pre-CTOPP Print Knowledge, complex language PLS-4, early math CMA-DE) plus social-emotional/behavioral and teacher-child relationship and teacher-behavior outcomes. Coded in the meta-analysis as Teacher/Class RCT, Pre-k, Low SES, Comprehensive approaches (the 'Pre-k' label is a slight mismatch: the sample is toddler-age center-based care).
problems: MULTI-ARM (3-arm) cluster RCT: business-as-usual control vs RECC vs RECC+ (RECC plus explicit social-emotional supplement). The paper's primary inferential contrast was the AVERAGE of the two intervention groups vs control (a priori orthogonal contrasts), plus RECC-vs-RECC+; it did NOT report a separate RECC-vs-control or RECC+-vs-control impact coefficient for cognitive outcomes. Per spec I extract the program-PD-vs-control contrast for each intervention arm separately, labelled by arm. CRITICAL DATA LIMITATION: the article reports NO numeric impact estimate, SE, or effect size for ANY child cognitive/achievement outcome -- the text explicitly states 'No significant group differences were found for growth in children's vocabulary (EOWPVT), early literacy (Pre-CTOPP), complex language (PLS-4), or math knowledge (CMA-DE)' (p.534-535), and Table 3 gives ONLY per-condition means/SDs by time point with no n per arm and no effect sizes. (Numeric effect sizes in the paper are reported only for teacher behaviors [Table 2] and for social-emotional / teacher-child-relationship outcomes, which are out of scope per spec.) The paper's own effect-size convention (Hess & Olejnik 2001) was the pre-post change difference (treatment minus control) divided by the control baseline SD -- NOT reported numerically for cognitive outcomes. THEREFORE the g values below are MY OWN computation of an UNADJUSTED post-test (Time 3) standardized mean difference (treatment arm minus control), standardized by the pooled posttest SD; they are NOT the pretest-adjusted growth-model estimates the study used and NOT the paper's gain-score effect size. They also do not match the study's analytic contrast (which combined both intervention arms). PER-ARM n NOT REPORTED: Table 3 gives only a total N per outcome (Vocabulary N=493, Early Literacy N=490, Complex Language N=492, Early Math N=490, maximum observations); per-condition child n and the analyzed per-arm classroom n are not in this PDF, so n_t/n_c are null and g_var/g_se are ROUGH estimates assuming n/arm = total_N/3 (recorded only as approximate; flagged in notes). CLUSTER ADJUSTMENT: cluster_adjusted=false (my g is from child-level raw means/SDs); the design ICCs are in online Appendix F, NOT in this PDF, so icc is left null (never guessed) and n_clusters per arm is unknown (~20/arm). BASELINE IMBALANCE: Time 1 (Wave 1) means in Table 3 show some imbalance (e.g., early math T1 RECC 16.23 vs control 19.09; complex language T1 RECC 3.06 vs control 4.04), which is exactly why the authors used gain-score effect sizes and pretest-adjusted growth models; the unadjusted posttest g understates the treatment position on math/language where control started higher. ATTRITION was high (43% classroom teacher turnover; 26% child attrition). Bottom line: the meta-analytic 'TPD vs business-as-usual on child achievement' contrast for this study is, per the authors, NULL across all four cognitive domains; numbers below are best-available reconstructed posttest SMDs flagged low-precision.

effect_sizes.arm_label: RECC (Responsive Early Childhood Curriculum + responsive-teaching PD/coaching) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.g_method: Computed by extractor: d = (M_RECC - M_control)/SD_pooled at Time 3, J small-sample correction (df estimated from N/3 per arm). Standardized by pooled posttest SD. NOT pretest-adjusted; NOT the paper's gain-score/growth-model estimate (paper reported none for cognitive outcomes).
effect_sizes.notes: Authors report this contrast as NON-significant ('no significant group differences ... for growth in vocabulary'). Per-arm n not given (total N=493); g_var/g_se are rough (assume n/arm ~164). Time1 (baseline) M(SD): RECC 15.60(9.69), control 17.55(10.01) -- slight control advantage at baseline.
